propositions: Batch overlap-judge candidates in a single call per ordering instead of one call per candidate, reducing N=6 candidates from 12 calls to 2 calls and eliminating ~8,460 token-equivalents of repeated system prefix overhead.

Lift the stable system prompt prefix from 873 tokens to 1,337 tokens by adding a batch protocol section, crossing the 1024-token cache floor and enabling prompt caching, resulting in 1,331 cached tokens.

Reduce total input tokens from 18,494 (8415 baseline) to 9,116 on an identical real corpus, a net 50.7% improvement against 8415 and 48.1% versus pre-8415, validated by real anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 API measurement.
Demultiplex batched verdicts by label rather than position, ensuring an absent or malformed batch entry causes abstain only for that candidate and leaves other verdicts intact.

Verdict relation labels shift systematically on 6/12 ordered pairs toward conservative outcomes (related_distinct→unrelated, depends_on→related_distinct), reproducible across runs but no true-positive recall loss observed in positive-control test.
Judge batching stays advisory with fail-safe semantics: a raising runner or malformed batched response yields empty list from judge() with no exception propagation.
